x-inventory-kind: Confirmed current Selectel Swift subset; normalized bulk query selector; headers/query variants share primitive binding, inventory completeness unknown

x-disposition.auth: IAM project X-Auth-Token only; not S3SigV4 or legacy Swift auth.
x-disposition.inventory: Current account/container/object method-path primitives plus bulk-delete query selector; metadata/limits share POST bindings, upload/copy-from/DLO/SLO/symlink share PUT binding with explicit source-confirmed variants. No duplicate coverage for convenience aliases.
x-disposition.stream: Binary upload/download use explicit reader/writer, TransferTimeout, byte bounds, no full buffering and no implicit replay. Known segment locators/manifests explicit; no discovery/adoption or automatic segment creation.
source_discrepancies: Account quota table says X-Container-Meta-Quota-Bytes, but description and explicit account example use X-Account-Meta-Quota-Bytes; choose the repeated account-specific example, never scope-shift container header.
Object metadata table says X-Container-Meta but object example uses X-Object-Meta-Some; retain source evidence and choose explicit object header.
Some response examples incorrectly say X-Openstack-Requiest-Id; canonical documented header plus X-Trans-Id are allowlisted, do not echo arbitrary headers.

Most endpoint table rows include /v1 while kz-1 row lacks it; API examples consistently wire /v1/{project_id}. Normalize confirmed service version once, preserve exact host, do not guess different domain.
Bulk-delete example uses single-quoted Python-like notation despite JSON format; decoder accepts the documented compatible JSON wire shape only, never eval or quote rewriting.
x-disposition.continued_variants: Current Selectel plain listings plus compatible core Swift XML list format; pinned listing_formats.py resolves exact XML shapes. Already-confirmed Selectel multipart-manifest=delete accepts documented204 acknowledgement and source-bound compatible SLO200 JSON bulk summary; pinned slo.py+bulk.py resolve status and body. This does not assert a specific provider deployment revision or support for unmentioned upstream features.
x-disposition.upstream_boundary: The pinned upstream revision is compatible wire-shape evidence, not the Selectel deployment revision. New optional upstream features (SLO range/inline data/heartbeat/async, additional listing properties, and unrequested middleware APIs) are not silently admitted to the Selectel inventory. Only current Selectel-confirmed methods/selectors are bound; XML/plain representations and the JSON SLO delete response are decoded using the pinned compatible protocol implementation.
